cards.text: Jesus has just finished teaching up on the mountain (Matthew 5:1-7:29). Now He comes down, and large crowds follow Him. Friend, the biggest crowd I ever drew was the family whose kitchen I lived in, and they were there for the cookie dough, not me.
Suddenly, a man with leprosy comes and kneels before Jesus. No appointment, no heads-up, just SUDDENLY.

cards.question: The man with leprosy kneels before Jesus and calls Him Lord. What does he say Jesus can do for him?
The leper asks Jesus to make him clean. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: He reaches out and touches him
He tells him to wash in the Jordan
He puts mud on his skin

cards.text: Then Jesus answers him: “I am willing… Be clean!”

cards.question: Jesus says “Be clean!” and the leper's healing takes a few days to finish.

cards.text: Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS waiting for somebody to remember me, and this man waits zero seconds. Then Jesus instructs him, “See that you don’t tell anyone.”

cards.question: Jesus tells the man He healed of leprosy not to tell anyone. But he's to go and show himself to the ___.

cards.text: The man is also to offer the gift prescribed by Moses, Israel's lawgiver, as a testimony to them. Then Jesus enters Capernaum, and a centurion, an army officer, comes and pleads with Him.

cards.question: The centurion in Capernaum pleads with Jesus. Who is he asking for help for?

cards.text: He says, “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.” I bet this one has been keeping him up at night.

cards.question: When the centurion tells Him about his servant, Jesus says He will go and heal him.

cards.text: Jesus is ready to head over. Then the centurion answers, and friend… I did NOT see this coming.

cards.question: The centurion tells Jesus he is not worthy. Not worthy of what?

answers.text: Having Jesus come under his roof

cards.question: So the centurion asks for something else. He asks Jesus to just say the ___, and his servant will be healed.

cards.text: Then he explains that he's a man under authority, with soldiers under him: he tells one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. Friend, I tell my oven timer to stop, and it beeps LOUDER.

cards.question: Why does the centurion tell Jesus about the soldiers and the servant under him?

answers.text: He knows a command gets obeyed
He wants Jesus to see his rank
He offers his men to guard Jesus

cards.text: Jesus hears what the centurion said, and He marvels. Then He turns to the people following Him.

cards.question: Jesus turns to the people following Him. What does He say about the centurion's faith?

answers.text: He hasn't found faith this great in Israel
It's as small as a mustard seed for now
It will grow if he keeps on asking

cards.text: Then Jesus says many will come from the east and the west. They'll gather with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Israel's forefathers, in the kingdom of heaven.

cards.question: Many will come from the east and the west. What will they share with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven?

cards.text: But Jesus also says the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

cards.question: Then Jesus turns back to the centurion and tells him to go. It will be done for him just as he has ___.
The centurion's servant is healed at that very hour.

cards.text: Next, Jesus arrives at the house of Peter, one of His disciples. He sees Peter's mother-in-law sick in bed with a fever.
So He touches her hand, and the fever leaves her. Friend, when I touch somebody's hand, all they get is flour on it.

cards.question: The fever leaves Peter's mother-in-law. What does she do next?

answers.text: She gets up and serves Him
She runs to tell the neighbors

cards.text: When evening comes, many who are demon-possessed are brought to Jesus. He drives out the spirits with a word.

cards.question: That evening, Jesus heals some of the sick who are brought to Him, but not all of them.
After telling about that evening, the writer says this was to fulfill words spoken long before. Who spoke them?

cards.text: The writer quotes Isaiah 53:4: “He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases.” Friend, let that one sit with you a minute.
